correctness.rationale: For each displayed code the deterministic verifier constructs every distinct ordered two-symbol descendant of every four-symbol codeword and confirms that all 81 ordered pairs over the nine-symbol alphabet occur exactly once. This is exactly the perfectness criterion. Published bounds and constructions independently supply DL(9,4)=14 and known sizes 18 and 19.

evidence: Chee–Ge–Ling Theorems 7.18 and 7.28 retain q=9 as a possible exception to the complete length-four spectrum.

broader_coverage.reasoning: The strongest inspected general results give the interval and the optimum but do not imply membership of 16 or 17 in the spectrum.

evidence: Published existence at sizes 18 and 19 is explicit.
Perfect deletion-code spectra are not automatically contiguous; the spectrum problem exists precisely because different sizes require constructions or exclusions.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: Existence of larger perfect codes does not imply existence of smaller perfect codes. The explicit size-16 and size-17 partitions therefore add statements not entailed by the cited 18- and 19-word constructions.

evidence: Chee–Ge–Ling Proposition 3.4 identifies perfect length-four two-deletion codes with perfect directed packings DP(q,4).
The displayed codeword lists were compared under both terminologies.
equivalent_formulations.reasoning: The claim is invariant under the deletion-code/directed-packing equivalence, so a prior result in either vocabulary would cover it; none was located in the inspected sources.

originality.rationale: The 2010 full-spectrum paper leaves q=9 unresolved, the cited Wang paper determines only the optimal size, and targeted checks under both deletion-code and directed-packing terminology found no inspected source giving the two explicit memberships 16 and 17.
residual_risks: An obscure, non-indexed, or differently termed earlier construction of one of the two codes may exist; database non-detection is not a mathematical proof of novelty.
